obligations.text: A `case_regressions` clause passes only when every compared case has a known value on both sides and the number of regressing cases is at most `at_most`; a case with a measure on one side only, a measure missing from some run of a side, or an unknown or non-finite value makes the clause unknown unless the definite regressions already exceed `at_most`, and it is never counted as a pass, a non-regression or a regression by default.

Whether a case regresses is decided in exact decimal: the baseline and candidate case values are taken as the shortest decimals that round-trip to their binary64 values and `by` as its exact decimal, and a case worse by exactly `by` regresses.
A selection gate that does not use `case_regressions` has the same canonical bytes and identity as today, and `gate select` over it writes the same `rustev.selection/1` bytes, stdout and exit code.

sectionHeadings: 064: Selection gate: a clause on per-case regressions against the baseline (amends 029 and 061)
record.summary: An amendment of approved specs 029 (3.12) and 061 (3.7), for release 0.6.0 (#537), ratified by the owner on 2026-11-06 (A-83). Every selection clause today compares `pooled` values of the cohort `all` or of each slice, so a candidate that improves most cases and collapses on a few passes `not_worse_than`. This spec adds one clause to `rustev.selection-gate/1`, `case_regressions`, which counts the dataset cases whose candidate value is worse than their baseline value by at least a declared absolute amount, in the metric's declared direction, and fails when more than a declared number regress. A case's value is 029 3.3.3's `pooled` computation restricted to that case, read from the per-case documents the baseline and each candidate already bind (`rustev.eval-cases/1`, or 061's `rustev.host-cases/1`), so no baseline document changes. The boundary is compared in exact decimal; a missing, partial or unknown case value makes the clause unknown, never a pass; `rustev.selection/1` lists the regressing cases. Gates and selections that do not use the clause keep their bytes and identities.
